summary:
Vacation! The right time to implement a few old ideas. My interior design has now been completed (wardrobe). So something a bit more daring — since the whole thing seems to work, it’s time to document the result.

The Idea

PowerPoint and projectors are no longer anything special these days. Impress? Well…

It’s time for something new again. And as always, when you’re lacking creativity, you simply reach for something old to suggest something new. With this tried-and-tested method, the author does not want to be an exception.
title: The Beginning

summary:
The working material has arrived: two projectors and about 500 slides! The projectors are a Braun Paximat and a Rollei P355 .

The Paximat is the older and thus more representative one, the Rollei “faster” and therefore well suited for viewing and cataloguing.

Special thanks at this point also go to the generous donor, the flea market expert and slide enthusiast Thomas Heinemann!
title: The Equipment

summary: The window of a slide mount has a size of 36mm x 24mm. To insert the foils from PowerPoint, a corresponding template is needed. The template below was created with InDesign — the PDF files that can be produced with PowerPoint fit nicely into it.
title: The Template

summary:
The author received about 500 slides together with the projectors. How do you get an overview of them? How do you find the right motifs? Unfortunately there is only one way: look at all of them…

A setup made of a webcam and a projector lends itself to this, see below.

The next step is then to manage and tag the images in a suitable program.

The first choice was supposed to be Picasa — the Windows version also offers capture via webcam. Unfortunately it was not possible to make this version work with the webcam under Wine or VirtualBox . Under VirtualBox, a five-year-old bug stood in the way.
title: Getting an Overview

summary: The experiment needs content. I thought for a long time about what it could be — at one point the idea was to bring together several other old ideas for a database and turn them into a concept (in one of the previous posts I linked to Google, because the Rollei P 355 has no URI, this urgently needs to be changed!), but considering the vacation about to end, that was too ambitious. So the first presentation will be an introduction of the very idea pursued here, which will also show what is actually feasible. Hence the following requirements for the first slide presentation:

summary:
Here are the first two “foils”:

Findings:

  • Grey doesn’t work.
  • Anything below font size 26 in PowerPoint doesn’t work.
  • Plastic mounts are the best suited.
  • You don’t need to leave a margin in PowerPoint.

title: New Slides and Slide Mounts

summary:
After a " mishap" on the part of my landlord’s property management brought me to the Göttingen recycling yard for the first time today, I can understand more and more the fascination for the supposedly old, for the “garbage”. So my collection now includes motifs on the theme of starting school, presumably from the early 90s. As well as the work of probably two photographers:

  • Travel pictures from Greece and the Alps, with an interest in aeroplanes, probably their own VW bus, the concrete bunkers emerging at the time, and massive overexposure. Hard to date, 70s or 80s
  • A similar period, though rather underexposed, family pictures

The former is of course particularly well suited for presenting text in front of it, the latter might be usable as an in-between image…
